verdict.tagline: Gorgeous fighting action hampered by steep prices and clunky menus.
for_you_if: you want stylish anime action with a booming soundtrack
you enjoy learning deep fighting game mechanics
not_for_you_if: you expect a full character roster without extra purchases
you struggle with input registration on standard controllers

cohorts.summary: Reviewers highlight locked characters, non-interactive story scenes, and difficult menus, alongside steep learning curves.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that a large portion of the character roster is locked behind paid downloadable content while the base game includes a smaller selection of characters.

citations.review_text:
over 50% of the roster is paywalled, even character colors are paywalled. Many specials are straight up taken out, hardly any combo carryover whatsoever from previous entries. 

Close enough, welcome back blazblue cross tag battle.

Great fighter, really bizarre decisions though.

Story mode once again like xrd is just a multi hour anime movie that's about as well done as berserk 2017 with zero love put into it. Probably not that bad, but holy christ the pacing is definitely the worst thing about it and when you have the fighting animations to compare everything to, it's incredibly disappointing. I fail to see why having a few cpu fights here and there for situations would have been bad, but I guess I'm the crazy one since this is the second time they've done it.

I think the biggest issue though is easily the roster. I love the characters don't get me wrong, but it's absolutely disgusting to spend even 20$ on sale for the base game and see that you only have access to 15 of the 34 characters iirc the selection screen. It doesn't help that old favorites like baiken, testsment, ABA, Johnny, aren't part of the default roster despite heavily recurring in most titles only to be shoved out of the way to make you pay an extra fee to get them back. Maybe this wouldn't be nearly as bad if I were just picking up the game on release, but the fact the game never goes below 20 while demanding you spend an extra 115$ to get the actual full game isn't okay in any context, especially if you'll forcibly make the player fight these characters in the arcade mode when they don't have access.

It's all mearly enough to make me not recommend, but also it's fundamentally a real fun fighting game with fantastic animations, art direction and music which is all that really matters I suppose, even despite the nightmarish monetization and a story shoved in the trash bin in the corner of the game.

No offense to all the people that play this game, but what joy are you feeling from this game? I feel like the UI is super clunky, unpolished, and some of it unnecessary. I also think the main menu is hard to navigate. Another thing you should think about before purchasing this game is how many dlc characters there are compared to free characters. As of writing this there are 36 playable characters, the latest being Jam Kuradoberi. 15 of these characters are free to play when you buy the base game, that means there is 21 paid characters. That is crazy. These characters aren't very expensive so anyone buying this game should be able to buy 1 or 2 characters that appeal to them. This game isnt all bad though, the art style and ost are amazing, very balanced characters, and really fun. Despite all these good things it doesnt do it for me, shortly before writing this review I was playing Street Fighter 6 for the first time. Already way better in my opinion, I also play tekken 8. Also really fun
Good game but nontheless there's 17 7$ characters in a 40$ game but it does go on sale

This is a fighting game made by people trying to show off just how much they can do. And it's too much.

You got so many system mechanics. "Roman cancels" and "counter blitz" and "wild assault" like bro, I get it, I'm very impressed. But you know what would really impress me? A training mode with usable UI. There's no cohesive vision of what the game is meant to be. They add and remove full system mechanics willy-nilly.

 It's basically trying to be a high-tier kusogame with every character having over-the-top BS, which I respect, but what that boils down to is most of its players are just gonna mash buttons and use their strong options, like "Totsugeki". Tutorialisation is godawful and it's got typical Arcsystemworks "learn long combo strings off the internet" over any actual structure for learning how to string combos together.

As for single player content? Story mode? "Make 'em watch a movie".
 
But hey, we've got style, right? "KO"? Heh, we say "Slash!" when you win a match. Why? Idk, so terminally-online memesters can be insufferable about how ToTeZ rAd the game.

Speaking of the playerbase, I tried out the matchmaking and I was getting put up against super high level players who teabag when they beat a level 0 player. Eventually got a decent match against a similar-level player but it was the exception. Shame.

I'm sure if you've got the time to learn a mile-long list of system mechanics in order to get to the kusogame, there's some fun to be had, it's just not for me. On a base level, trying to make combos just feels bad and clunky, and most of the appeal — the visuals and presentation — is buried because the gameplay is a confused, undulating mess that you'd only dive into if you didn't know any better. Play SF6, Killer Instinct, hell even DBFZ knows what it is.

Guilty Gear is the fighting game equivalent of the guy who uses big words in a YouTube essay to seem smarter than he actually is. You have to learn a bunch of highfalutin concepts only to go in and…

claims.claim: Reviewers describe encountering unresponsive controls or input registration issues when playing on keyboards and standard controllers.

citations.review_text:
pure ass compared to xrd, or accent core.... hell i will call overture better game than this,  oversimplified thing for disabled people (worse than tekken 8).

- no insta kills

- ruining buttons for keyboard players (try to play happy chaos on keyboard). extremly ass registration on keyboard, which makes you miss inputs. kof 2002 um and 98 got same issues, but damn they older than guilty gear itself.
not mentioning a weird phantom lag when you try to pull one move, but game decides (for example if you press -d, it will not registrate down + right, instead it will do Down - Right - Up. How? i have zero idea too

- spam spam spam, on xrd spamming was extremly punishable. on accent core it was uneffictive for many reasons. but here, use zato or sin and you literally will be unpunished, only if you don't do stupid mistakes. (and yes i remember xrd2 sin, but running into someone who really knows how to play him was extremy rare and maybe only on japanese arcades)

- removing half of moves from characters. i have zero idea who's idea was that but i only see spamming ♥♥♥♥ like sin, ky and axl

- ranked. holy, i have zero idea how as new happy chaos for example must play against 12k rp dizzy or last rank giovanna, who's obviously demolish me. not speaking of 200 - 420 ms every game.

summorizing all this ♥♥♥♥, if you are new player just miss this game or try older titles, this game just don't worth it.

If you don't have top dollar accessories the game feels like it's actively fighting you on it's inputs. Why does pressing Y on a controller equals B sometimes? Idk. Why does half circle then forward makes a neutral? I Don't Know. Not to mention the actual loop, you only play the same 2 or 3 combos, and that's being generous since half the time the game functions as an unskippable cutscene and a waste of time depending on who you're playing and playing against. If it wasn't for the fact my friend bought this game for me, I wouldn't play it. If i wanted unresponsive gameplay and time wasted, I'd play a game off of itch.io; at least then any input would be used to make the game a bit better than just getting the usual "yeah, the game just does that." As in WHY is that the answer, why is the second one getting a dedicated controller. Not to mention the characters that feel like actual "pay to win." Why should I be paying this casually with friends if the game is constantly saying its for comp play; get good or get out. 

TLDR or don't care: Unresponsive at a Lot of the time, get good at the same 2 or 3 combos that everyone uses on the Combo Search/Youtube and try not to sink money in a what feels like a faulty character system.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight that matches feature dynamic anime-style graphics and distinct character designs, alongside a prominent rock soundtrack.

citations.review_text:
Honestly a really fun fighting game. The characters and animations look incredible, and the whole game has a really unique anime style that makes the fights feel much more exciting.

I also really like how unique the characters are. They all have their own abilities, playstyles and combos, so finding a character that suits you is a big part of the fun.

The combat is satisfying once you start getting the hang of the combos. There's definitely a learning curve, especially if you're not used to fighting games, but pulling off a combo you've been practising feels great.

My main negative is that it can be pretty overwhelming at first, especially with how much there is to learn. Some of the more advanced mechanics take a while to understand, and getting destroyed by experienced players online can be frustrating.

Overall though, I'm really enjoying it. Great graphics, awesome character designs and satisfying combat make it easy to recommend, especially if you enjoy anime-style fighting games.

Oh and the soundtrack is the cherry on top.

Hey kiddo, Handsome Jack here... and I just played Guilty Gear Strive, and apparently somebody decided that fighting games weren't complicated enough, so they added heavy metal, giant swords, magic, vampires, robots, and people dressed like they lost a bet. And honestly? Fantastic. You pick a character, walk into a match, and within approximately four seconds you're being launched across the screen by a guy carrying a sword the size of a telephone pole. Very normal. Very balanced. Probably how the military intended combat to work.

And the characters? Oh, they're incredible. You've got a walking nuclear disaster, a cowboy with a gun, a man who is somehow also a dolphin enthusiast, a literal vampire, and a guy who looks like he hasn't slept since 1997. Everyone has some horrifying backstory involving war, governments, experiments, gods, or the complete collapse of civilization. Meanwhile I'm just trying to figure out why my opponent has decided I don't get to touch the ground anymore.

Then there's the music. THE MUSIC. Kiddo, this game doesn't have a soundtrack. It has a personal vendetta against silence. Every fight sounds like I'm headlining the world's angriest rock concert while two superpowered lunatics beat each other to death in front of me. I could lose every single match and still walk away feeling like I just witnessed something historically important.

And somehow the game makes you want to get better. You lose, you stare at the screen, you tell yourself you're never playing again, and five minutes later you're back because you are absolutely convinced that this time you're going to destroy that smug little bastard who perfected the combo that ruined your evening.

10/10, kiddo. Gorgeous, ridiculous, insanely stylish, and loud enough to wake the dead. I'd give it an 11, but apparently the developers decided that letting me win every match would be “bad game design.” Which is a fascinating way to say they're jealous of my talent.

I highly recommend this game to anyone that loves fighting games, rock music, and willing to learn new things. I love playing Faust, and a little May. But the game in it of itself is Very Fun, it's Soundtrack is great, the art style is dynamic, colorful, and sharp. Basically, I'd say this game is great. It's not the most perfect game ever, but it's a fun time if you like fun characters, good gameplay, rock music, and fighting games.

citations.review_text:
Imo one of the best fighting games right now, the art style and animation is unrivaled and all the characters are fantastic, both in their designs and gameplay. Also one of the best soundtracks in gaming, the memes that say "it's a free album with a game included" speak as to how great the music is. This game is big but I'd say deserves even more attention! 
My only issue with the game is the overall cost, the $40 base game is reasonable but $25 for each season pass after 1 is way too much for only four characters per pass

i really want to enjoy this game, like i really do, the characters are all pretty good, the ost is top notch, it's really fun to learn the characters and use them, but what the hell is all this dlc and battlepass doodoo

before all of that i remember having up to the season pass 4 dlc, i was kinda blinded by how fun and unique the gameplay was (pretty fun and beginner friendly to a degree). i tried climbing the ranks, hit a roadblock due to CERTAIN. CHARACTER. MAINS. (bridget, elphelt and slayer), but the other matches against other characters were all very fun

some characters, however, need some emergency nerfs or just make them require actual learning their moveset instead of spamming the same move in hopes to win (like potemkin to a degree, bridget and elphelt, probably slayer too because he's just button mashing). it's just not fun at all to fight against people that use the same ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ combo and win effortlessly

overall i'll give the game a 4.5/10, not bad, but has very major flaws that overshadow the rest

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight problems with PlayStation controller support, noting that turning off the Steam input manager causes the game to fail to register inputs or requires mods to display correct button prompts.

citations.review_text: Great game,only issue is that the store page says that there is full PlayStation controller support but when steam input manager is turned off it doesn't take inputs from the controller (So don't use a PlayStation controller as steam input manager in my experience is very bad and constantly drops my inputs as well as turns my inputs into completely different inputs), also requiring a mod to even see which button does what (Note this is not an issue with Xbox controllers to my knowledge as I do not own one I cannot check).

As a person who is more new to fighting games, Guilty Gear Strive is genuinely so cool.

This is a LONG review (brace yourself)

One of the first fighting games I enjoyed (as of 2025-2026) was 2XKO and so transitioning from that to GGS was definitely confusing, in other words if you’re a person who prefers modern controls it’s gonna be a bit of a hurdle to get used to the controls BUT MORE THAN POSSIBLE! 

The controls are not intuitive at first considering they are more traditional (having punch, kick, slash, and heavy slash) and motion controls (quarter circles and Half circles). But asking the community in the discussion about these are really useful! 

And not only that The games support for a variety of controllers made it much easier for me to enjoy the game! (Hitbkx, leverless, controller, AND EVEN KEYBOARD!!!) A controller was tough for my thumb but using a keyboard made putting inputs way easier after getting used to the layout!

I thought I would need a dictionary worth of guides but turns out a single 15-30 minute video (depending on what you choose to watch) can cover a lot of the basics!  Of course with every fighting game it’s important to learn the fundamentals. But learning is where it s the most fun, since there’s tons of tools for you to help, from combo trials, training and lab, and even being able to save replays from when you verse people! The hurdle to play this game wasn’t big as I made it out to be. 

My best advice is to not put intense pressure on yourself to learn and DO NOT BE AFRAID TO ASK FOR HELP OR SEARCH UP GUIDES. 

But NOW ONTO THE ACTUAL GAME. 

. The art style being a 3D with the most 2D style I’ve seen is eye candy

And of course CHARACTERS LOOK AMAZING. Every single person has one heck of a personality just by their looks. 

I personally main Anji just cause I thought he looks cool and was 3 stars ease of use (btw the game lets you know how easy a character is to use by 5 stars. 1 being really difficult, and 5 being beginner fr…

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the user interface and non-ranked online modes outside of actual matches as awkward, slow, and unintuitive.

citations.review_text: You can raise a child in between these queue times and genuinely nobody plays anything but ranked but when you actually do get a game it's pretty good when you know how to play the game.

Once you're in a match this game is fantastic: streamlined systems with good balance and excellent netcode. Best experience I've ever had with Guilty Gear, having played Xrd and ACR before.

The game slowly connects to servers on launch... for no good reason, since it has to connect again once you're actually playing online anyway. Also the main way to actually get matches is "Ranked Mode", NOT quick tower or anything else; the other "unique" online modes are just awkward and annoying to use.

This is a very good game which suffers from unintuitive annoyances outside of matches, but those issues are genuinely minor. Stupid that these issues exist at all, and unlikely to be fixed because they're probably hard-coded at a foundational level of Strive's programming, but these issues are genuinely minor. If you're willing to learn a game as difficult as Guilty Gear, you'll learn how to navigate these menu annoyances easily enough

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes training missions designed to help players learn the systems.

citations.review_text:
I've never played a fighting game before, this one is awesome.  The animations are incredible and the character design is so interesting, so I found it easy to stay engaged while I learned how to use my buttons.  People say this game is simple, idek what that means but it's definitely a great first fighting game.  I felt comfy here after a couple hours and one youtube video and I just hit silver after 25 hours.

DO THE MISSIONS ITS THE TUTORIAL

Best fighting game around. It can feel slow, weird, clunky when you first boot it up, but there are a ton of mechanics that make fights faster and more furious as you learn more and more tricks. And so many characters have really unique mechanics that you won't find in other fighters. This is the one.

If you're new to fighters or it's been a while, there's a whole series of training missions to help you incrementally learn the systems, from newbie up to the pro ♥♥♥♥ you see them doing at EVO.

Game is 5 years old but average wait to find a ranked match is 10 seconds. The 2.0 overhaul a few months ago was huge and brought a lot of great stuff to the game, it's the best time to get into the game. The 2.0 Starter Edition is the best bang for your buck, you get all the characters for less than buying everything one at a time, even at discounts.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the single-player content is lacking, describing the story mode as an anime movie with little of the game's animation budget.

citations.review_text:
Strive is a game that has come a very long way from it's release version. Characters have more to do and still retain their unique playstyles for the most part. Do their Xrd and AC counterparts have more options? Yes of course they do but a good enough amount of freedom has been gained over the years.

This is still by far the best looking modern fighting game to me. Character visual designs are complex but so cohesive that they appear simple at first and no other series even approaches Guilty Gear's style. Soundtrack is amazing, Daisuke really just flexing how strong and flexible a composer he is.

If you are not a fighting game player I'll say it is very hard to find videos of people not just thinking every single character looks cool and fun as hell. But there is not a ton to do single player wise. There is a story mode but its basically a like 5 hour anime movie which got very little of the game's animation budget. 

If you are a fighting game player I think the vast majority of players will find a character who's playstyle you vibe with or at the very least one that is so cool or speaks to you personally well enough to get you to learn a new playstyle. And Strive takes you from fighting the character to fighting the player pretty quickly.

I decided to finally give fighting games a serious try and learn how to properly play them. This was the one I chose for the task.
So far so good. Gameplay feels tight but precise. I sometimes have to fight with myself to correctly imput some stuff, but that's just a skill issue on my part. I'm having quite a lot of fun. Currently hardstuck at gold and maining Johnny.
The music and visual aspects of the game are top tier, of course. Can't comment on the story yet cause I keep posponing the 4 or so hour movie.
Some people complain about the blazing pass but I personally couldn't care less about it. Paid cosmetics have been a thing in Japanese games since forever so to me it's whatever.
Overall, great game. Even as a full noob I've had a good online experience. For anyone who's also new, I suggest jumping straight into ranked(after learning your basic moves in training and with some wikies of course) because that's where I've been matched with people of my skill around 95% of the time. The tower and park and lobbies don't have proper matchmaking so you'll struggle to find fair fights there.

citations.review_text:
I had to completely stop playing Guilty Gear -STRIVE- for personal reasons, but it's actually a really solid fighting game. Before the last major update I would not have been able to say this, but ArcSys has really undertaken to make their game better, and more fair, and less snowball-y, and to give it a good ranked system, better training tools, and many other little things. That's just the gameplay, by the way.

In terms of everything else, GGST is a master class: one of the best video game OSTs of all time, right up there with greats like the Persona franchise; incredible lore sprawling over decades and numerous media formats; best-in-class visual art direction, non-music sound direction (including voice acting), and overall creativity. 

I really cannot sing the praises of Strive (and Guilty Gear as a whole) quite enough. My main issue is that I feel like Strive has, in some respect, lost the Guilty Gear way by adding more and more modern monetization schemes. This started with DLC characters, maps, etc., but the value there, both artistically and commercially, is high and clear. The pricing on the individual items is insane, but I think that's just to encourage you to buy the (reasonably priced) bundles. The thing that really put a bitter taste in my mouth (and put the last nail in the coffin for me to stop playing) was the battle pass; I can't fully express why I hate this so much, but it just feels *wrong* for the game that's so cool, and built around being so cool, to implement a strategy which I (and many) see as flagrant nickel-and-diming for trash, like an urchin peddling plastic ankhs to tourists. However, I really like to believe that this is just ArcSys experimenting rather than knowingly, intentionally selling out, but I doubt anything will change given it's probably been a financial success.

This is a lot of kvetching over a game which I still rate positively; this is because I know my complaints are very specific and most people do not care, doubly…

I love guilty gear. I didn't really mind much when they were charging to expand the roster.. much..

But they added a battle pass? I know I'm late to the party on that info but BRUH lol

I normally avoid mobile games and ones with battle passes because I hate FOMO and limited time paid content with a burning passion. I also have hated every other fighter game I've played. Strive unfortunately has really fun characters, I say unfortunately because the characters I like to play are almost constantly in the bottom tiers whilst the less complicated ones I find brain dead and boring are top tier. That wouldn't have warrented a negative review but given they already charge a hefty sum to buy the base game plus all the DLC, (at the moment the "starter edition" is $128 in my native currency.) But now they've added paid battle passes. I want to play this game but with this battle pass being a constant reminder of how most games by big publishers are just about draining your bank account as much as possible I never close the game in a good mood. Is it fun? It definately can be. Are there better things to do with $60-130? Yes, definately.

The majority of the cast is DLC. Maps are DLC. Colours are DLC.

Can't training mode against characters you don't own.

Oh and now there is a battle pass too.

Genuinely such a huge disappointment;
A fun game ruined by greed
Say No to battle passes

[b] If youre a casual fighting game player then this game is great! 

If youre a competitive player, then the game is kinda good? [/b]

[h1] If youre a competitive player...[/h1]
[h3] Game balance [/h3]
The main concern if you're a competitive player will always be the balance of the game. I think its well known that update 2.0 is generally positivly recieved, however this isnt to say that it fixed the balance of the game, far from it actually. 

Sadely, the strongest characters from season 4 (Anji, Pot, May, Leo, Ram, Goldlewis) are still the strongest in the game today, despite practically running the game for almost 3 years now. The update also boosted other characters such as Zato and Nago, making them now extremely unfun to fight due to their explosive capablities, or  easy-to-secure win condition. 

The balance of the game might be better than it was in season 4, however its just demoralizing that these characters are still problematic, 2 years later. 

[h3] The replay system [/h3]
Another massive issue this game has is the lack of a actual good replay system. In older Guilty Gear games, you could use something called "replay takeover" which allowed you pick anywhere in the replay, and start playing in that spot to practice! This feature also appears in SF6, however in Strive its gone. 

Furthermore, the replay system does not allow you to view frame data, nor rewind! If you wanted to re-watch a moment that you didnt understand, you have to replay the entire round from the start. Just being able to go back like 3 seconds would be amazing! Unfortently, its been 5 years since the game has released and this complaint is well known, so I dont see them addressing it anytime soon.

[h3] Equal Skilled Prolonged Sets are a pain to set p [/h3]
